attribution.note: The parenthetical spoiler is Marcus's own aside, added to his summary of Kording's worry. It is his assertion, not a quotation of Kording.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully states that current approaches to machine causal reasoning are not yet adequate, and it keeps the 'not yet' qualifier. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Marcus gives no adequacy threshold. Reading 'adequate' as dependable, broadly useful causal reasoning is an ordinary, fair reading. Setting the period to December 2022 is reasonable. The result still depends on how broadly 'adequate' is read.

evidence.note: The December 2022 revision of a preprint finds language-model causal answers sensitive to wording, alongside partial successes. It covers few models and no field-wide test, so it does not establish broad inadequacy.

Neural causal models can identify and estimate causal effects under structural assumptions in simulation. This is a narrow success and does not show dependable causal reasoning across varied problems.

reviews.rationale: Neither condition is met. e1 shows mixed language-model results with limited coverage. e2 is a narrow success under assumptions. The contract says isolated failures or narrow successes cannot settle the claim, and no evaluation covering the relevant approaches as of December 2022 is in the packet.

attribution.note: Marcus frames this as what the speakers could agree on, but he was one of the speakers and adopts the view in his own voice. 'I think' qualifies the consensus, not the forecast.

semantics.note: 'Is about to have a huge impact' is firm, unhedged language about a near-term outcome. The 'current form' qualifier is kept as scope. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Reading 'huge impact' as mass uptake plus substantial institutional or practical change is ordinary and fair. Reading 'current form' as the kinds of AI then emerging, rather than frozen model versions, matches the speaker's point that this AI is not AGI.

evidence.note: A representative survey (August 2024) finds 39.4% generative-AI adoption among US adults aged 18–64, with 28.1% of workers using it at work. This shows mass uptake within about 20 months of the post.

The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. It is an enacted, EU-wide framework that covers chatbots and general-purpose models. The source is an official record of the event, not a self-assessment.
Only 18% of US adults had used ChatGPT by July 2023. This covers one product at an earlier date. It tempers claims of immediate uptake but does not rule out the later impact.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule names a major enacted regulatory framework plus representative evidence of widespread use. Both appear by August 2024: the EU AI Act in force (e4) and 39.4% adoption (e3). e5 shows lower earlier uptake but does not negate this. The result depends on the contract's reading of 'huge impact'.
